_doc: Per-shot EXPOSURE trims, applied to a shot's own segment before the film's grade. A still that arrives brighter than the shot beside it breaks the cut: two frames of the same room at the same hour read as two mornings. This is the only per-shot move the studio makes, and it is exposure only.
_rule: A gain in LINEAR light, applied identically to R, G and B. That scales luminance and leaves chromaticity where it was. A gain above 1 is refused by lib/grade.js outright - lightening is the colourism defect the grade exists to prevent, and no continuity argument outranks it. Bring the brighter shot down; never lift the darker one.
_never: A trim is not a grade. It cannot warm, cool, saturate, or touch a face on its own. The film's grade runs on top of it unchanged, and tools/gradecheck.js still measures the locked skin albedo through the whole chain afterwards.

trims.reason: The approved 01-01 arrives about 20% brighter than 01-02 - measured YAVG 118.66 against 100.96 on the scaled 1080x1920 frames. 01-01 cuts straight to 01-02 and they are the same hall at the same hour, so the brightness reads as a second morning. Venkat, 2026-09-22: 'bring it down to sit with 01-02 so the cut reads as one room, one morning. Don't change its colour, only its exposure.'

measured.how: solved by bisection on the real filter, not estimated from the ratio - a display-space ratio of 0.851 is a 0.6773 gain in linear light
measured.colour_held: linear channel means all scaled 0.670-0.672; R:G moved 2.03881 -> 2.04242 and B:G 0.49355 -> 0.49251, both under a quarter of one percent, which is 8-bit LUT quantisation and not a colour move
